turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell regarded Miss Fairfax's interruption with a look of profound disapproval, then turned her attention back to Mr. Worthing. turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack stammered slightly, attempting a reassuring smile. turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell arched a perfectly sculpted eyebrow, regarding Mr. Worthing with a mixture of amusement and thinly veiled disapproval. turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen, with a delicate shudder, declared that the particulars of trades were utterly vulgar and quite beside the point; surely, Mother understood that a gentleman's character was demonstrated by his affections, not by the inventory of his family's shop.

turns.speaker: Jack

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell regarded Mr. Worthing with an expression of profound skepticism, her lips curving into a barely perceptible smile. turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack shifted uncomfortably, a blush rising on his cheeks. turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell regarded Jack with a chillingly polite air, her gaze unwavering. turns.speaker: Jack

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen, with a delicate sigh and a pointed glance at Jack, declared that while she appreciated her mother's diligence, surely a gentleman’s character was best assessed not by a relentless interrogation of his parentage, but by the sincerity of his affection. turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack, feeling a desperate need to regain some ground, hastened to agree with Gwendolen, insisting that, of course, affection was paramount, and he hoped his actions demonstrated the depth of his regard for her. turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell raised a perfectly sculpted eyebrow, her gaze sweeping over Jack with an air of profound skepticism. turns.speaker: Gwendolen

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell regarded Gwendolen's sentiment with a degree of polite disdain, then turned her attention back to Mr. Worthing, her expression suggesting that sincerity and devotion were, alas, quite secondary to demonstrable pedigree.
